blueprint_topic: Management of Care — advance care planning, self-determination, and future-care preferences in heart failure
stem: A nurse is participating in advance care planning with a client who has heart failure. Which action best reflects the purpose of this process?

options.A: Invite the client to describe values, goals, and future-care preferences, discuss surrogate designation, and plan to revisit these choices as circumstances evolve.
options.B: Document the client's current treatment preferences in an advance directive and revisit them mainly when the medical treatment plan changes substantially.
options.C: Ask the client to name a surrogate and have that person define future treatment preferences while the client focuses on current heart-failure management.
options.D: Center the discussion on resuscitation status and defer broader values and goals until heart-failure progression makes end-of-life decisions more immediate.

rationale: A is correct. Section 13.1 of the 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA heart-failure guideline defines advance care planning as a process that supports understanding and sharing a patient's personal values, life goals, and preferences regarding future medical care. Key domains include discussing values, documenting plans for medical treatments, designating a surrogate decision maker, and revisiting the process over time. B is incorrect because advance care planning is an ongoing process rather than documentation that is revisited mainly after a major treatment-plan change. C is incorrect because surrogate designation supports future decision-making but does not displace the capable client's own values and preferences. D is incorrect because advance care planning is broader than resuscitation status and need not wait until end-of-life decisions become immediate.
educational_objective: Use advance care planning as an ongoing client-centered process for communicating values, goals and future-care preferences, designating a surrogate, and revisiting the plan over time.
source_organization: American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology/Heart Failure Society of America
source_document_title: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure

blueprint_locator: Appendix A — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care, printed page 20/PDF file page 24: Advance Directives/Self-Determination/Life Planning — assess knowledge of advance directives, integrate advance directives into the plan of care, and provide information about advance directives/self-determination/life planning; Advocacy — discuss treatment options with the client and respect decisions; Client Rights — recognize right to refuse and discuss treatment options/decisions with the client. Management of Care activity statements also include integrating advance directives into the plan of care and verifying client education/consent.
pdf_visual_verification: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan printed page 20/PDF file page 24 was visually verified by screenshot on 2026-08-20; Advance Directives/Self-Determination/Life Planning, Advocacy, Case Management, and Client Rights content was visible with no CACHE MISS.

correction_summary: Retained the advance-care-planning construct but removed the 'only CPR' and one-time-form cueing. The revised distractors test realistic errors involving infrequent reassessment, premature transfer of decision-making to a surrogate, and delayed/broadly narrowed goals discussion.

option_audit.A: Correct; directly integrates values/goals/preferences, surrogate designation, and revisiting over time from Section 13.1.
option_audit.B: Plausible documentation-centered error; incorrect because ongoing ACP is broader than revisiting a document mainly after major treatment changes.
option_audit.C: Plausible surrogate-role error; incorrect because naming a surrogate does not transfer current decision authority away from a capable client.
option_audit.D: Plausible code-status/end-stage framing error; incorrect because ACP is broader than resuscitation decisions and can occur before end-of-life decisions become immediate.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on always/never/only/all/must-type absolutes.
cueing_audit.answer_length: All four alternatives contain comparable planning detail; the key is not uniquely signaled by length.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four alternatives are parallel advance-care-planning actions.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified after AHA/ACC/HFSA and NCSBN source-based reread.
